svg.title: Medical Courier Launch Sequence
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-courier-launch-sequence; chapter number: 1; title: Medical Courier Launch Sequence; subtitle: Contract first, vehicle second, reserves before direct invoicing; chart type: process_flow; stages: step: 01; label: Land the contract before the vehicle; value: Step 1; detail: No van or Sprinter purchase until a signed contract covers the payment; the car already owned is the launch vehicle (Medical Courier Connection).; step: 02; label: Carry HIPAA and bloodborne pathogen training; value: Step 2; detail: Practitioners treat HIPAA and bloodborne pathogen training as the baseline credential for any medical courier route.; step: 03; label: Bind commercial auto plus business liability; value: Step 3; detail: Diamond Hunter Enterprises: commercial auto insurance plus business liability insurance, even as a solo operator.; step: 04; label: Bank three months of operating expenses; value: Step 4; detail: Invoice-paid direct clients run 20-30 day billing cycles and first checks can take 90 days (Medical Courier Connection).; step: 05; label: Hire a driver only at a $300-$500 weekly spread; value: Step 5; detail: Hire only when $300-$500 a week remains after driver pay, and check the client contract for subcontractor and approval clauses first (Giganomic Era).; caption: The launch order practitioners converge on: contract, credentials, insurance, cash reserves, then the first hire.; assumptions note: Sequence reflects the operator gates as stated; Sarah Davis notes that at levels one and two a name, SSN and 1099 status were enough to get hired before any LLC or EIN.; note: Sources - Medical Courier Connection (o1VRiVMJTpY @ 00:24:07, 00:14:00); Diamond Hunter Enterprises (zQaL3OdQ2D8 @ 00:04:29); Giganomic Era (2w9s8G4Gx9Q @ 00:00:41).
